drhp.business:
EAAA India Alternatives Limited (EDELALTS) is an India-based alternative investment platform with a multi-thousand crore AUM base in total AUM and fee-paying AUM (FPAUM) as of June 30, 2026. FPAUM grew at a CAGR over the last three fiscal years.

The company operates two main business verticals. Real Assets invests in infrastructure and commercial real estate via a mix of equity, quasi-equity and debt instruments. Its sub-strategies are Infrastructure Yield (launched FY2018), Commercial Real Estate Yield (FY2024), Perpetual Capital (FY2023), and Energy Transition (FY2026); this vertical managed 10 Active Funds including two InvITs, with FPAUM of ₹280,399.05 million as of June 30, 2026. Private Credit provides credit and flexible financing solutions across Performing Credit (launched FY2010), Special Situations (FY2012), Real Estate Credit (FY2016), and Investment Grade Credit (FY2018); this vertical managed 16 Active Funds with FPAUM of ₹192,724.16 million. A third bucket (Others) covers Portfolio Management Services (PMS) and co-investment structures, with combined FPAUM of ₹13,108.55 million.

Over the last three fiscal years and Q1 FY2027, the company raised capital commitments of ₹475,262.50 million, deployed ₹382,293.99 million and realised investments of ₹312,329.40 million. As of June 30, 2026, the company managed 11,009 client relationships globally, of which 1,493 are repeat clients (having invested in more than one fund); 77% of AUM is committed by repeat clients. The institutional client share (pension funds, insurance companies, banks) is 49.32%, with 50.68% from non-institutional clients (UHNIs, HNIs, family offices, corporates). The company has offices in Mumbai, New Delhi, GIFT City and Singapore, with coverage extending to North America, Europe, Middle East, Japan, Australia and South Korea.

Wholly owned subsidiary Sekura India Management Limited acts as the asset operating and management team and holds accreditations under ISO 14001:2015, ISO 45001:2018, ISO/IEC 27001:2022 and ISO 55001:2014. As of June 30, 2026, the team comprises 85 investment professionals, 58 Sekura members (asset ops), 13 coverage members and 108 enterprise staff.

overview.business_overview:
We are one of the leading alternatives platforms in India, in terms of assets under management (“AUM”) with more than 17 years of experience (Source: CARE Report) of managing long term patient capital with an AUM of ₹953,448.78 million, as of June 30, 2026. Our key business verticals include: (i) real assets (“Real Assets”), which invests in a mix of equity, quasi-equity and debt instruments and (ii) private credit (“Private Credit”), which primarily invests in debt or convertible debt instruments and secular instruments for superior risk adjusted returns. Our wholly owned subsidiary, Sekura India Management Limited (“Sekura”), is part of our — asset operating and management team and proficiently supports our various business verticals, including operations, maintenance, monitoring, efficiency improvement, and turnaround management. We are an experienced player, catering to a diverse client base of global and domestic institutional clients and manage India focused funds across our business verticals. As of June 30, 2026, our FPAUM totaled ₹486,231.76 million. Over last three financial years, our FPAUM grew at compounded annual growth rate (“CAGR”) of approximately 23.43% to ₹447,104.42 million in Financial Year 2026. Most of our large funds are in or entering in their third and fourth series, and we have consistently been able to raise capital across the series, indicating our ability to generate sustainable performance, maintain client confidence, and adapt to market conditions. In the last three Financial Years and the three months period ended June 30, 2026, we raised capital commitment aggregating to ₹475,262.50 million, deployed investments aggregating to ₹382,293.99 million and realized investments aggregating to ₹312,329.40 million. Most of our funds also have a track record of delivering strong performance consistently across different market cycles. Such strong realizations of our funds ensured the return of realized portion of NAV back to clients, thereby establishing a track record of delivering strong performance. We have invested significant time and resources over the years in building a global, scalable, coverage platform for a diverse client base including institutional investors, ultra-high net worth individuals (“UHNIs”), high net worth individuals (“HNIs”) and family offices. As of June 30, 2026, through the funds that we managed, we had 11,009 client relationships globally and in India, including 1,493 repeat clients (i.e., clients who have invested in more than one of our funds) and 8,800 clients added from April 1, 2023 to June 30, 2026. As of June 30, 2026, 77% of our AUM comprised of commitments made by our repeat clients, signifying the strength of our long-standing client relationships. This high percentage underscores the trust and confidence that our clients have in our platform and investment strategies, as well as our consistent ability to deliver performance and maintain client satisfaction over time. We have a diverse client base; approximately 49.32% of our AUM is contributed by institutional clients as of June 30, 2026, including pension funds, insurance companies, banks etc., while the remaining 50.68% is contributed by non-institutional clients (including UHNIs/HNIs and family offices, corporate and others etc.). Additionally, as of June 30, 2026, our client base extends to multiple geographies globally including India, North America and Europe. Our presence in Mumbai, New Delhi, GIFT City and Singapore ensures on ground coverage through our chaperoning partners and relationship managers, covering North America, Europe, Middle East, Japan, Australia and South Korea. This also offers us flexibility to create solutions for both onshore and offshore clientele.

As of the date of this Red Herring Prospectus, our business verticals include:

• Real Assets – Our Real Assets business vertical, invests into infrastructure and commercial real estate (“Infrastructure and Commercial Real Estate”) assets with low counterparty risk, long residual tenures, through a mix of equity, quasi-equity and debt instruments. Our Real Assets sub-vertical include:

(i) infrastructure yield (“Infrastructure Yield”) (first launched in Financial Year 2018), (ii) commercial real estate yield (“Commercial Real Estate Yield”) (first launched in Financial Year 2024), (iii) perpetual capital (“Perpetual Capital”) (first launched in Financial Year 2023), and (iv) energy transition (“Energy Transition”) (launched in Financial Year 2026). Our Real Assets verticals focus on revenue enhancement through increasing operational efficiency, cost optimization and, creating portfolios and enhancing returns by exiting them as a portfolio. As of June 30, 2026, our Real Assets business vertical managed 10 Active Funds which includes two Infrastructure Investment Trusts (“InvITs”), with a FPAUM of ₹280,399.05 million.

• Private Credit – Our Private Credit business vertical, provide credit and flexible financing solutions across the risk spectrum and possess the necessary capabilities to source, structure, manage, and exit investments. Our Private Credit sub-vertical include: (i) performing credit (“Performing Credit”) (first launched in Financial Year 2010), (ii) special situations (“Special Situations”) (first launched in Financial Year 2012), (iii) real estate credit (“Real Estate Credit”) (first launched in Financial Year 2016), and (iv) Investment Grade credit (“IG Credit”) (first launched in Financial Year 2018). As of June 30, 2026, our Private Credit business vertical managed 16 Active Funds, with a FPAUM of ₹192,724.16 million.

• Others – We also offer other business verticals and services, including, portfolio management services (“PMS”) and others. Our PMS provide co-investment opportunities to our clients. As of June 30, 2026, the combined FPAUM of other verticals was ₹13,108.55 million.

(5) Active Funds includes funds, Co-Investment PMS and InvITs managed / advised by the Company and its Subsidiaries, that are either accepting capital, making new investments, or managing their portfolio of assets, excluding the special purpose funds. We are led by our management team which has extensive experience in asset management, investment and risk management functions and are backed by a qualified and independent board. The senior management team comprises individuals who have been associated with the entities listed under our Promoter and its subsidiaries for an average of about 5.45 years. Our strategies are executed by our key teams: our investment team, asset operating and management team, coverage team and enterprise team.

Additionally, Sekura ensures adherence of portfolio company to applicable technical, safety, health, and environment, and risk management protocols, aligned with industry practices and are validated through independent ISO audits and accreditations, such as ISO 14001:2015 (for environment management system), ISO 45001:2018 (for occupational health and safety management system), ISO/IEC 27001:2022 (for information security management system), and ISO 55001:2014 (for asset management system). Further, Sekura’s transport vehicle laboratory, the Transportation Engineering Research and Excellence Centre (TEREC) located at Turbhe, has been accredited by the National Accreditation Board for Testing and Calibration Laboratories (NABL) in accordance with ISO/IEC 17025:2017.

As of June 30, 2026, (i) our investment team included 85 experienced professionals, responsible for sourcing transactions across our verticals; (ii) our asset operating and management team, operated through Sekura, included 58 members, focusing on portfolio management, value enhancement, technology and process development, sales and cash flow monitoring, asset optimization, and turnaround of our investee companies, led by Sekura’s management team with extensive industry experience. Our coverage team includes 13 members, with extensive global and domestic reach, is instrumental in building our diversified client base across multiple geographies and our enterprise team includes 108 members, for the performance of various corporate functions of our business, such as risk management, governance and compliance.

Furthermore, we have implemented a comprehensive risk management framework. At the company level, risk monitoring practices ensure proactive identification and management of existing and emerging risks. With respect to our business verticals, we conduct risk assessments at various stages of investment, including activities such as asset review, regular risk monitoring, risk categorization and valuation. We regularly monitor and conduct risk-based classification of our funds’ portfolio assets to mitigate risk exposure and ensure alignment with fund documents, processes and global best practices in environmental, social, and governance (“ESG”) criteria. We are also one of the few signatories in India to the United Nations-supported Principles for Responsible Investment, since January 2023. This commitment underscores our dedication to integrating ESG factors into our investment strategies, enhancing our reputation among clients and stakeholders, who prioritize responsible investment practices.

Additionally, our private credit vertical won the “IVCA Best Overall Performance of the Year – Private Credit Fund” award at the Alternative Capital Excellence Awards by the Indian Venture Capital Association both times in 2025 and 2024, and the title of “Private Debt Investor (PDI) – Top Private Debt Fund Raisers” by Private Debt Investor five times in 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024 and 2025. Furthermore, we were conferred with the “Asian Investor – Asset Management Award and Market Awards – India Category” award at the Asian Investor Asset Management Awards both times in 2025 and 2024, the “Indian Alternatives Investment Thought Leadership, 2024 Award” in Operational Category by Equalifi in 2024, and the “Best BFSI Brand” at the ETNOW Best BFSI Brands, 2024. Additionally, we are recognized as the “Top 2 India Infrastructure Investor, 2024” Infrastructure Investor. We have also been recognized as one of the “Prestigious Brands of Asia 2025” by the process evaluators and research panel, the BARC Asia & Jury at the Global Symposium 2025. Furthermore, we have been awarded the Asset Management Company of the Year in India by the Global Private Banker Innovation Awards 2025. We also received the Gold Award for Annual Report 2025 at the Spotlight Awards for Global Communications 2024 – 2025 by the League of American Communication Professionals (“LACP”) and the Gold Award for Annual Report 2023 by LACP, in the category of Financial Diversified Services. At GenAI Conclave and Awards 2025, we received “Best Gen AI Use Case of the Year” and “Best Implementation for Gen AI for Business 2025” and in 2024, we won the “GenAI: Initiative of the Year 2024 Award” at GenAI Conclave & Awards 2024, UBS Forums. We have also won “Best Overall Performance of the Year - Infrastructure Funds” award at the IVCA Alternate Capital Excellence Awards 2026, the Asian Investor Asset Management Award in the Market Category for India for three consecutive years in 2024, 2025 and 2026, the Gold Award and Technical Award for the Company’s Annual Report 2024-25 at the LACP Vision Awards 2025, the Gold Award for the Company’s Annual Report 2023-24 at the Spotlight Awards for Global Communications by LACP, and the Gold Award for the Company’s Annual Report 2022-23 by LACP in the Financial Diversified Services category.

We derive our Total Income primarily from three income streams: (i) Management and Advisory Fees; (ii) Variable Additional Return; and (iii) GP Income. The chart below sets forth the breakdown of our income streams:

(i) Management and Advisory Fees: Management and Advisory Fee is the fee received for providing management and advisory services. Management and Advisory Fee is generally charged as a percentage of capital committed, capital invested, net asset value (“NAV”), gross block etc. Our Management and Advisory Fees stream is notably stable, largely stemming from multi-year contractual agreements.

(ii) Variable Additional Return: Variable Additional Return is the additional variable return to the Company and its Subsidiaries once the fund has achieved the hurdle rate of return for its investors based on NAV and/or Realisation, shown as other operating revenues in Restated Consolidated Financial Information. The recognition of Variable Additional Return is guided by the waterfall distribution mechanism specified in the respective fund documentation and as per Company and its Subsidiaries’ policies. Variable Additional Return is the additional return on sponsor or general partner commitment, which is dependent on the performance of our funds. Based on the guidance under the Ind AS and the current policy that we adopted for recognition of Variable Additional Return, Variable Additional Return is recognized in our books of accounts after a minimum of three years from its initial close date. It is also contingent upon the fund’s performance achieving at least 1.25 times the hurdle rate specified in the respective fund documents at the time of recognition of Variable Additional Return. According to the waterfall mechanism specified in each fund document, and subject to the above conditions, Variable Additional Return is calculated and recognized over the remaining life of the respective funds up to the expected date of the first realisation and as per Company’s policy.

(iii) GP Income: GP Income refers to income on investments in funds or co-investing in portfolio companies, on the same terms as the primary fund. It is calculated as sum of Interest income on debt instruments/ Pass through certificates and Net Gain / (Loss) on fair value changes from investments in AIF/ Debt Instrument / Pass through certificate / equity forming part of other income in the Restated Consolidated Financial Information. General partner and/or sponsor investments reflect our alignment of interests with clients by using our capital in the funds or co-investing in portfolio companies, on the same terms as the primary fund. ‘GP Income’ represents the income on these investments.

(1) Management and Advisory fee is the fee received for providing management and advisory services. Management and Advisory Fee is generally charged as a percentage of capital committed, capital invested, net asset value, gross block etc as per respective governing documents.

(2) Variable Additional Return is the additional variable return to the Company and its Subsidiaries once the fund has achieved the hurdle rate of return for its investors based on NAV and/or Realisation, shown as other operating revenues in Restated Consolidated Financial Information. The recognition of Variable Additional Return is guided by the waterfall distribution mechanism specified in the respective fund documentation and as per Company and its Subsidiaries’ policies.

Out of the cumulative Variable Additional Return of ₹6,847.20 million recognised by our Company from Financial Year 2024 up to the three-month period ended 30 June 2026, an amount of ₹3,976.54 million has been realized. business_model.title: Business (RHP)
business_model.body:
EAAA India Alternatives Limited (EDELALTS) is an India-based alternative investment platform with a multi-thousand crore AUM base in total AUM and fee-paying AUM (FPAUM) as of June 30, 2026. FPAUM grew at a CAGR over the last three fiscal years.

The company operates two main business verticals. Real Assets invests in infrastructure and commercial real estate via a mix of equity, quasi-equity and debt instruments. Its sub-strategies are Infrastructure Yield (launched FY2018), Commercial Real Estate Yield (FY2024), Perpetual Capital (FY2023), and Energy Transition (FY2026); this vertical managed 10 Active Funds including two InvITs, with FPAUM of ₹280,399.05 million as of June 30, 2026. Private Credit provides credit and flexible financing solutions across Performing Credit (launched FY2010), Special Situations (FY2012), Real Estate Credit (FY2016), and Investment Grade Credit (FY2018); this vertical managed 16 Active Funds with FPAUM of ₹192,724.16 million. A third bucket (Others) covers Portfolio Management Services (PMS) and co-investment structures, with combined FPAUM of ₹13,108.55 million.

Over the last three fiscal years and Q1 FY2027, the company raised capital commitments of ₹475,262.50 million, deployed ₹382,293.99 million and realised investments of ₹312,329.40 million. As of June 30, 2026, the company managed 11,009 client relationships globally, of which 1,493 are repeat clients (having invested in more than one fund); 77% of AUM is committed by repeat clients. The institutional client share (pension funds, insurance companies, banks) is 49.32%, with 50.68% from non-institutional clients (UHNIs, HNIs, family offices, corporates). The company has offices in Mumbai, New Delhi, GIFT City and Singapore, with coverage extending to North America, Europe, Middle East, Japan, Australia and South Korea.

Wholly owned subsidiary Sekura India Management Limited acts as the asset operating and management team and holds accreditations under ISO 14001:2015, ISO 45001:2018, ISO/IEC 27001:2022 and ISO 55001:2014. As of June 30, 2026, the team comprises 85 investment professionals, 58 Sekura members (asset ops), 13 coverage members and 108 enterprise staff.
